paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So let's go back to the human world. We're just talking about pens — this is an easy thing to talk about. What is it about your mind and body, that container, that allows certain seeds to ripen and other seeds not to ripen? Well, there’s not much kindness. What I’m saying is that, if there are certain conditions in place, certain seeds will never ripen within them.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: If there's not certain conditions in your identity — the person that you see yourself as, automatically — then certain seeds will not be able to ripen.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Like the guy sitting next to me on the airplane. The script that is running in his mind, the person that he is, arises as the seeds that are arising as him — a person that sees a world that is empty, lack, doesn't have enough resources, and he himself will never have the things that he actually wants.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Now, if we were in a different class, in a different place, we'd be like: just change your view, and change your affirmations, and then you'll feel better about yourself, and then you'll get all the money you want. I hope that doesn't go online. I didn't mean it quite so sarcastically. But I said it.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: It's not just about changing your thoughts about yourself. That's what I mean.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: But if your script is automatic — the script of who you are is automatically arising in a certain way — you're only going to have certain seeds available in those conditions.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: That boy of 15 years ago, the one that Gina showed you — that boy saw things in a certain way. And so his world ripened in that way. And even all the seeds he was trying to plant — until he removed certain things about himself, he was still going to keep believing that, and his world was going to be that way.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Now you can understand a little bit more clearly how difficult this really is. Because we're not just planting seeds for more money, or for good relationships. Yes, keep freaking doing all those things. Don't stop. Keep being kind. Keep being generous. I'm not saying stop. But you want to create the conditions for those seeds to ripen in. You want to create the postal delivery service.

chapters.title: The View You Have of Yourself

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So if you use the metaphor of the human and the dog, and apply that to you — there's a you. Because objectively speaking, was I ugly, or was I hot? Some people would say yes, some people would say no, both directions. That's why there are 8 billion people on the planet. Someone will like you. But do you like you? I didn't like myself. And that was a form of renunciation. There has to be a different way, because I see a lot of people who do love themselves, and it doesn't matter how much money they have. Of course, I want a lot of money, and I want to love myself, and I want the best relationships.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: That person had certain ways that he was believing himself to be, that confirmed the world that he saw. All relationships are the same. They're all going to end the same. Nobody loves me. Nobody wants me. It's all going to end. No one's going to love me for who I am. If you arise that way, what world is going to present? What kind of partners are you going to attract? The ones that like this part of you, but don't like this part of you. They love you when you're like this, but they don't love the other part of you. And when they don't love you, you go — well, of course no one's going to love all of me. Of course, it's always happened that way.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Years ago, I asked my teacher a very important question. I said, “Look…” I didn’t say, “Look.” I was much more respectful. In my mind. I said, I don't think my problem is going to be solved by going to the nursing home. I don't feel lonely in that way. I have companionship when I want it. Tengo a todos mis amigos Mexicanos.

paragraphs.speaker: Interpreter
paragraphs.text: I have all my Mexican buddies.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I always have them. They're always there, regardless of how grumpy I am. They surround me, and they jump, and they hug me, and they're like, just keep going. And then eventually I get happy, right? And secretly, I love it. Because I want to feel that myself. Like, I don't want to feel lonely and separated. Because I didn't feel that all of me is lovable. But they've shown me that I am. But it doesn't matter what other people tell you. It's the belief that comes from within.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So what we're going to investigate is: we're going to look at ourselves, and what are those limiting beliefs that we have? Those things that we go, I am like this, it is always like this, and it's never going to change. How many people say those words in their head, in some variety of "it's always going to be this way"? And then the world confirms it.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And then guess what you're doing when you do that? And then what else you’re doing. Not only are you planting that seed, in the technical definition of the word — you are tartukeando, tartuking.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: You are giving fertilizer. You are planting that seed, and it's germinating all the time, and you don't even know you're doing it. Because you, as you, is doing it. And you don’t even know you’re doing it.. That flow of seeds of your mind and body is just flowing that. If you could change the flow of your mind and body — that thing that you call Tim — it's just a seed opening up. It's just a different seed.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: We have lifetimes of habits. But on the other side of it, we have a very unique opportunity. And that unique opportunity is the fact that we were born a human. Because a dog cannot think this way. You might be stuck in some limited belief in your life, might be stuck in some way. But part of that package of the mind and body that we have as a human is that we can actually think about it. We can actually observe it. We can actually shine a light on those blind spots. Because if you change you, you change the seeds that are possible. And so the question becomes: how do we start shining that light? Without going into a total psychological breakdown.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: When I saw that picture, and I saw the difference of who I am now than I was 15 years ago, I told you that I went through a grief process.

paragraphs.speaker: Interpreter
paragraphs.text: Les dije que pasé por un proceso como de luto.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: That was the word I was looking for. A deep grief, because I was like, oh my God, how much of life did I waste being that person? Like, how much pain did I cause myself and others being that person? And you can go there. And I highly recommend not. {laughs} But there's also an emotional component to all of these things too. For me — this is Tim saying this, this is not the ancient text saying this, I just want to clarify — I have found that when I go to those places and I truly feel all of those emotions, and then I can see what motivated them, as that person, say 15 years ago — that for me is purification. Because I don't need to go back there again.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And then the other point of view that arises is that I'm grateful for him. Because he was also a cause for who I am. So was that person a total failure, a total negative loss 15 years ago? No.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: And this is what I'm going to leave you with tonight, and then tomorrow we're going to dive a little deeper into it.
